title_en: New Slang, New Stories (20/20): Old Coworkers Reunite Three Years Later
note_en: The particle 过 after a verb marks something you have experienced at some point: 有人“躺平”过，有人“摆烂”过 "some had lain flat, some had let it rot." It works like English "have done (at some point)," but unlike English it attaches straight to the verb, even a slang word like 破防过 or emo过, and the verb itself never changes form.

sentences.en: At the reunion, someone brought up that group PowerPoint assignment that had nearly driven everyone over the edge. The classmates who had pulled all-nighters revising it more than ten times for the sake of involution had all gone their separate ways, and word was that one of them was now a project manager and was the first to tell newcomers, "Don't get caught in the rat race. Efficiency matters more than overtime."

sentences.en: Someone asked about Xiao Wu, who used to talk about "running" all the time and studied foreign languages and visa policies for different countries whenever he had the chance. He had come to the reunion too, and as they chatted it turned out he had never actually emigrated; he had just moved to a company with a healthier pace. But he really had worked his way through those foreign-language textbooks, and now he even picked up some freelance translation work from time to time.

sentences.en: Xiao Wan and A Qiang came together, too. The shekong girl who had once hidden in the corner at the year-end party could now tell jokes to the whole table on her own. A Qiang teased that she had "leveled up from shekong player to half a sheniu," and Xiao Wan shot back that at most she was "a sheniu at work, a shekong in life."
